Density and CDF plots of the estimated distribution of effects

Source: R/plot-g.R
plot_g.Rd

plot_g() plots the estimate of \(g\), the distribution of the true effects: its density, its cumulative distribution function (CDF) or its probabilities on the grid. The posterior mean is shown as a line and a pointwise posterior interval as a band. The estimates, a normal distribution, known true effects, individual posterior draws of \(g\) and other estimates of \(g\) can be added to the plot.

Usage

plot_g(
  x,
  type = c("density", "cdf", "mass"),
  level = 0.9,
  inner_level = NULL,
  observed = c("none", "histogram", "rug"),
  normal = FALSE,
  truth = NULL,
  draws = 0,
  compare = NULL,
  xlim = NULL,
  scale = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

type

What to plot: "density" (the default), "cdf" for the cumulative distribution function, or "mass" for the probabilities of the grid points. With "mass", only a rug of the estimates and posterior draws of \(g\) can be added to the plot.

level

Posterior probability of the pointwise band, a number between 0 and 1.

inner_level

Posterior probability of a second, darker band inside the first, a number between 0 and level. If NULL (the default), no inner band is shown.

observed

How to show the estimates: "none" (the default), "histogram" or "rug". When type = "cdf", "histogram" shows their empirical distribution function.

normal

If TRUE, the normal distribution described in Details is added. Can also be a numeric vector c(mean = , sd = ), which adds the normal distribution with that mean and standard deviation, in the units of the estimates.

truth

For simulated data, the true effects. A numeric vector is shown as a histogram (with type = "cdf", as an empirical distribution function). Can also be a function of the effect that returns the true density (with type = "cdf", the true distribution function). If NULL (the default), no true effects are shown.

draws

Number of individual posterior draws of \(g\) to add as thin lines, in addition to the posterior mean and the band. At most the number of draws in the fit can be shown.

compare

An optional named list of other estimates of \(g\), each plotted as one line. An element can be a bef_fit object or a data frame with a column x of effect values, in the units of the estimates, and a column density or cdf.

xlim

Limits of the horizontal axis, a numeric vector of length 2 in the units of the plot, i.e., after multiplication by scale. If NULL (the default), the limits are chosen as described in Details.

scale

Positive number by which effect values are multiplied and densities divided, e.g., scale = 100 to show differences in proportions as percentage points.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The line and the band are the columns mean, lower and upper returned by g_summary(). For point masses, the density is the probability of a grid point divided by the grid spacing, and the CDF spreads that probability evenly over the cell around the grid point.

The band is pointwise: the stated posterior probability applies to the curve at each effect value separately, not to the whole curve at once.

normal = TRUE adds the distribution of effects under the normal random-effects model, with its mean and standard deviation estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) from the same estimates. This is a plug-in estimate, shown as a single curve without a band, because the uncertainty in the estimated mean and standard deviation is ignored.

Note that a histogram of the estimates is not an estimate of \(g\). The estimates include sampling error, so they are more spread out than the true effects. The histogram shows the data to which the model was fitted.

The horizontal axis covers the grid unless the grid is much wider than the region where \(g\) has its mass, which would leave long empty stretches on both sides. If the central 99.9% of the posterior mean of \(g\) covers less than 60% of the grid, the axis is limited to that region plus a small margin. Use xlim to set other limits.

See also

g_summary(), plot_sites(), vignette("plots")

Examples

# The callback gaps in percentage points, with a histogram of the
# estimates and the normal distribution of the random-effects model.
plot_g(krw_fit, observed = "histogram", normal = TRUE, scale = 100)


# The distribution function, with a 50% band inside the 90% band.
plot_g(krw_fit, type = "cdf", inner_level = 0.5, scale = 100)


# Simulated sites with known true effects.
plot_g(twin_towers_fit, truth = twin_towers$theta_true, normal = TRUE)


# The posterior mean and band with 40 posterior draws of g.
plot_g(raudenbush_fit, draws = 40)
